title: Gorillaz Celebrate Mexico's 'Revolutionary Spirit' at Corona Capital
summary:
Gorillaz are back in Mexico City. On Friday, November 20, the British band headlined the first day of the Corona Capital festival, returning to the city for the first time in eight years. About 72,000 people packed the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, according to promoter Ocesa.

Frontman Damon Albarn praised Mexico's 'revolutionary spirit' from the stage. He also gave a shoutout to Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum, who had traveled in economy class to a summit in Shenzhen, China, the week before. Albarn called the choice an important statement, and he saluted the crowd.

The timing fit the occasion. Albarn spoke while wearing a red beret and a military-style jacket on Mexico's Revolution Day, observed every November 20 to mark the start of the 1910 uprising against Porfirio Díaz, who had ruled for more than 30 years.

The show was packed with special guests. Guitarist Johnny Marr joined the band for 'The Empty Dream Machine' and 'Casablanca,' songs he played on in the studio for Gorillaz's 2026 album The Mountain. He also performed 'The Plastic Guru' and 'The Sweet Prince.' Argentine rapper Trueno joined for 'THE MANIFESTO' and freestyled during 'Clint Eastwood,' the song that closed the set.

Mexican singer Luisa Almaguer joined for 'Latin Simone (¿Qué Pasa Contigo?),' a song from the band's 2001 debut album, in an emotional moment with the crowd. Singer Kara Jackson, U.S. rapper Bootie Brown, and MC Black Thought also took the stage. Other acts on the festival's first day included James Blake, Mumford & Sons, CHVRCHES, and The Kooks.
why_it_matters: Big concerts can also carry messages about a country's history and its leaders, and this show mixed music with a tribute to Mexico's Revolution Day.
